origin.description: Extract the first literal match from each string.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: Character vector of strings to search.

origin.details: The extracted text is the original substring, not the uppercased form. No match, an empty string, an empty pattern, or a missing value yields NA. A missing opts_fixed uses case-sensitive search without overlap. A dict may set case_insensitive and overlap. Case-insensitive search maps each code point with ICU u_toupper. A character whose uppercase form is longer than one code point is left unchanged, so ß does not match SS.
origin.value: A character vector. NA means there was no match.

translation.description: Extract the first literal match from each string.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: String, missing value, or list of those.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Literal pattern, missing value, or list of those.

arguments.name: opts_fixed
arguments.text: None, or a dict of search settings. Overlap is ignored.

arguments.name: case_insensitive
arguments.text: If given, match the simple uppercase of each code point.

arguments.name: overlap
arguments.text: Ignored, as in the installed function.

translation.details: The extracted text is the original substring, not the uppercased form. No match, an empty string, an empty pattern, or a missing value yields NA. A missing opts_fixed uses case-sensitive search without overlap. A dict may set case_insensitive and overlap. Case-insensitive search maps each code point with ICU u_toupper. translation.value: A list of strings and NA. NA means there was no match.
translation.example:
from stringi.fixed import stri_extract_first_fixed
found = stri_extract_first_fixed("ababa", "aba")
print(f'stri_extract_first_fixed("ababa", "aba") returns {found[0]}.')
